question: An incident ray passes through the focus of a concave mirror. The reflected ray:

options.text: is parallel to the principal axis
passes through the centre of curvature
passes through the focus of the mirror

solution:
The correct answer is __**is parallel to the principal axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An incident ray that passes through the focus of a concave mirror will reflect parallel to the principal axis.
 
• This is due to the property of concave mirrors where rays passing through the focus reflect parallel to the principal axis.
 
• The principal axis is the line that passes through the center of curvature and the focus, extending to infinity on both sides.
 
• This property is used in various optical devices to direct light in a specific direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror with a reflecting surface that curves inward.
 
• It is also known as a converging mirror because it converges light to a point.
 
 
 
• **Principal Axis:**
 
 
• The principal axis is a straight line that passes through the pole (the midpoint of the mirror) and the center of curvature of the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Focus (Focal Point):**
 
 
• The focus of a concave mirror is the point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to converge after reflecting off the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Center of Curvature:**
 
 
• The center of curvature is the center of the sphere of which the concave mirror is a part.
